title: Rumble Soars 10% on Report Anthropic Is the $13.7B Compute Customer; CoreWeave and Nebius Drop 9%
excerpt: A media report naming a marquee AI lab as the mystery customer behind Rumble's massive six-year compute contract is sending one small-cap stock sharply highe...
content_html:
Quick Read

  • Rumble surged 10% after a report named Anthropic as its $13.7B compute customer, while CoreWeave and Nebius each fell 9%.

  • Dario Amodei's call to slow AI development pressured rented-compute peers, as QQQ dropped 2% while cloud ETF SKYY held nearly flat.

  • The unconfirmed deal reportedly grants Anthropic an option to buy 51 million Rumble shares at $0.01, while the Georgia data center remains under construction.

  • Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Nebius Group didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat NBIS. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

Rumble (NASDAQ:RUM) stock is rising 10% to $7.87 in early Monday trading after a media report tied a marquee artificial intelligence (AI) customer to the six-year compute contract Rumble disclosed in an August securities filing. The pairing hasn't been confirmed by either party, but the reaction on Rumble stock has been immediate and directional. It's the kind of single-headline reprice a small-cap AI story rarely gets to enjoy on a red day for the trade.

The move is punishing the rented-compute peers on the same tape. CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) stock is down 9% to $81.25, and Nebius Group (NASDAQ:NBIS) stock is declining 9% to $205.28, extending recent softness in the group. The reported award reads as competitive share captured by Rumble at the peers' expense.

The framing check backs up that read. The First Trust Cloud Computing ETF (NASDAQ:SKYY) is down only 0.58%, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 1.63%. Today's damage is largely concentrated in AI-compute names rather than spread across cloud software, which puts Rumble's rally in sharper relief against a group being marked down.

Anthropic Report Fuels the Rally

According to a media report, the customer behind Rumble's $13.7 billion six-year compute contract is AI lab Anthropic, and the reported arrangement lets Anthropic acquire up to 51 million Rumble shares at $0.01 each. Rumble left the customer unnamed when it made the disclosure in August, and both companies remain silent on the pairing this morning. The capacity is expected to come from a Maysville, Georgia data center that is still under construction.
